text:
karthik: Heads-up — saw a regression on Mixtral-8 when serving chat templates. p99 up ~25% after the tokenizer bump. Anyone else?

nina: yep noticed on a few customer flows. looks correlated with messages that include emojis/curly quotes.

samir: any quick numbers?

karthik: perf snapshot from last night (live traffic):
```
model=Mixtral-8  config=opt-quant
baseline p99=120ms -> today p99=150ms (+25%)
CPU kernel switches: 3.2k -> 4.9k
KV cache miss rate: 0.9% -> 6.8%
byte-fallback token rate: 0.25% -> 3.9%
mean tokens per req: 34 -> 41 (because emoji/unicode expanded)
```

jin: interesting — byte-fallback increase explains token count jump. extra tokens increase KV size and triggers different kernel path (byte-optimized kernels) more often.

perf-bot: profile gist: https://perf.redwood/internal/17698-mixtral-chat-tokenburst (has per-kernel times)

nina: also saw RoPE scaling mismatch warnings in the kernel selector logs for Mixtral vs our default RoPE scale. it forced fallback to a slower generic attention for some seq-lens.

karthik: exact log: `rope_scale diff 1.024 != model_meta 1.0 -> kernel=generic_attn`

samir: so two issues compounding: tokenizer causing tokenburst and RoPE mismatch forcing generic kernels. both bloat KV activity and latency.

jin: quick mitigations: 1) enforce NFKC normalization + replace curly quotes/emojis in chat template sanitizer (pre-tokenize) 2) add a heuristic to prefer ropescale-compatible kernels when diff < 2% 3) detect high byte-fallback ratio and route to a variant with larger kv-cache batch size.

karthik: prototype patch pushed: https://phab/rD1234 (sanitizer + kernel threshold 0.02). rolling to canary.

perf-bot: canary numbers after sanitizer patch (1000 reqs):
```
byte-fallback rate -> 0.35%
mean tokens -> 35
p99 -> 125ms
kernel switch count -> 3.5k
KV miss -> 1.4%
```

nina: much better but p99 still +5% vs older baseline. suspect head/kv dim mismatch on a small subset of Mixtral variants — triggers slower matmul kernel.

samir: can we add a tiny runtime mapping that prefers kernels matching head*kv alignment (e.g., 64, 128) and fallback only if throughput would be worse?

jin: yes — kernel selector already records dims. we can weight by estimated GEMM efficiency. I can add a quick scoring function: score = latency_est * (1 + 0.02*kv_miss_rate).

karthik: also observed chat templates with leading BOS token cause cache invalidation across users because we include user_id in cache key in some routes. removing implicit BOS in templates recovered some cache hits.

nina: actionable checklist: 
- sanitize chat templates (NFKC, strip curly quotes, normalize emoji) [karthik]
- add 2% rope-scale tolerance to kernel selector [jin]
- add kernel scoring by head/kv alignment and kv-miss penalty [jin/samir]
- short-term: disable adding BOS to cache key for conversation-start route [samir]

samir: I’ll own cache key change and monitor for collisions.

karthik: load-testing plan: replay customer flows with injected emojis and curly quotes to validate. also run profiler to check the % time in attention kernels vs kv-copy.

perf-bot: add perf job: `jobs/eng-runtime/mixtral-tokenburst-replay` scheduled now. logs -> phab task rD1235.

jin: long-term idea: expose a 'tokenizer-safety' flag per model that triggers pre-tokenization normalization and routes to a tighter-kernel profile. Could be opt-in per customer.

nina: agreed. also add an alert: if byte-fallback_rate > 1% for 5m, fire pager for eng-runtime (warning).

karthik: thanks team. rolling canary for the kernel selector & sanitizer now. will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
